directives.name: admonition
directives.doc:
Callouts, or "admonitions", highlight a particular block of text that exists slightly apart from the narrative of your page, such as a note or a warning. 

 The admonition kind can be determined by the directive name used (e.g. `:::{tip}` or `:::{note}`).

arg.doc:
The optional title of the admonition, if not supplied the admonition kind will be used.

Note that the argument parsing is different from Sphinx, which does not allow named admonitions to have custom titles.

class.doc:
CSS classes to add to your admonition. Special classes include:

- `dropdown`: turns the admonition into a `<details>` html element
- `simple`: an admonition with "simple" styles
- the name of an admonition, the first valid admonition name encountered will be used (e.g. `tip`). Note that if you provide conflicting class names, the first valid admonition name will be used.

label.doc: Label the admonition to be cross-referenced or explicitly linked to.

enumerated.doc: Turn on/off the numbering for the specific admonition

icon.doc: Setting icon to false will hide the icon.

open.doc: Turn the admonition into a dropdown, if it isn't already, and set the open state.

body.doc: The body of the admonition. If there is no title and the body starts with bold text or a heading, that content will be used as the admonition title.

class.doc: Annotate the bibliography with a set of space-delimited class names.

label.doc: Label the bibliography to be cross-referenced or explicitly linked to.

enumerated.doc: Turn on/off the numbering for the specific bibliography

directives.name: csv-table
directives.doc: The "csv-table" directive is used to create a table from CSV (comma-separated values) data.

class.doc:
CSS classes to add to your table. Special classes include:

- `full-width`: changes the table environment to cover two columns in LaTeX

label.doc: Label the CSV table to be cross-referenced or explicitly linked to.

enumerated.doc: Turn on/off the numbering for the specific CSV table

enumerator.doc: Explicitly set the CSV table number

header.doc: Supplemental data for the table header, added independently of and before any header-rows from the main CSV data. Must use the same CSV format as the main CSV data.

header-rows.doc: The number of rows of CSV data to use in the table header. Defaults to 0.

delim.doc: The character used to separate data fields. The special values "tab" and "space" are converted to the respective whitespace characters. Defaults to "," (comma)

keepspace.doc: Treat whitespace immediately following the delimiter as significant. The default is to ignore such whitespace.

quote.doc:
The character used to quote fields containing special characters, such as the delimiter, quotes, or new-line characters. Must be a single character, defaults to `"` (a double quote)\
For example, `First cell, "These commas, for example, are escaped", Next cell`

escape.doc:
A character used to escape the delimiter or quote characters from the CSV parser. Must be a single character, defaults to `"` (a double quote) default is a double quote\
For example, `First cell, "These quotes"", for example, are escaped", Next cell`

directives.name: code
directives.doc: A code-block environment with a language as the argument, and options for highlighting, showing line numbers, and an optional filename.

class.doc: Annotate the code with a set of space-delimited class names.

label.doc: Label the code to be cross-referenced or explicitly linked to.

enumerated.doc: Turn on/off the numbering for the specific code

caption.doc: A parsed caption for the code block.

lineno-start.doc: Start line numbering from a particular value, default is 1. If present, line numbering is activated.

number-lines.doc: Alternative for "lineno-start", turns on line numbering and can be an integer that is the start of the line numbering.

emphasize-lines.doc: Emphasize particular lines (comma-separated numbers which can include ranges), e.g. "3,5,7-9"

filename.doc: Show the filename in addition to the rendered code. The `include` directive will use the filename by default, to turn off this default set the filename to `false`.

body.doc: The raw code to display for the code block.

arg.doc: Language for execution and display, for example `python`. It will default to the language of the notebook or containing markdown file.

class.doc: Annotate the code-cell with a set of space-delimited class names.

label.doc: Label the code-cell to be cross-referenced or explicitly linked to.

enumerated.doc: Turn on/off the numbering for the specific code-cell

emphasize-lines.doc: Emphasize particular lines (comma-separated numbers which can include ranges), e.g. "3,5,7-9"

tags.doc: A comma-separated list of tags to add to the cell, for example, `remove-input` or `hide-cell`.

body.doc: The code to be executed and displayed.

directives.name: embed
directives.doc: The embed directive allows you to duplicate content from another part of your project. This can also be done through the figure directive.

arg.doc: The label of the node that you are embedding.

class.doc: Annotate the embed with a set of space-delimited class names.

label.doc: Label the embed to be cross-referenced or explicitly linked to.

enumerated.doc: Turn on/off the numbering for the specific embed

remove-input.doc: If embedding a Jupyter Notebook cell, remove the input of the cell.

remove-output.doc: If embedding a Jupyter Notebook cell, remove the output of the cell.

directives.name: blockquote
directives.doc: Block quotes are used to indicate that the enclosed content forms an extended quotation. They may be followed by an inscription or attribution formed of a paragraph beginning with `--`, `---`, or an em-dash.

class.doc:
CSS classes to add to your blockquote. Special classes include:

- `pull-quote`: used for a blockquote node which should attract attention
- `epigraph`: used for a blockquote node that are usually found at the beginning of a document

label.doc: Label the blockquote to be cross-referenced or explicitly linked to.

enumerated.doc: Turn on/off the numbering for the specific blockquote

body.doc: The body of the quote, which may contain a special attribution paragraph that is turned into a caption

arg.doc: The filename of an image (e.g. `my-fig.png`), or an ID of a Jupyter Notebook cell (e.g. `#my-cell`).

class.doc:
CSS classes to add to your figure. Special classes include:

- `full-width`: changes the figure environment to cover two columns in LaTeX

label.doc: Label the figure to be cross-referenced or explicitly linked to.

enumerated.doc: Turn on/off the numbering for the specific figure

height.doc: The figure height, in CSS units, for example `4em` or `300px`.

width.doc: The figure width, in CSS units, for example `50%` or `300px`.

align.doc: The alignment of the image in the figure. Choose one of `left`, `center` or `right`

remove-input.doc: If the argument is a notebook cell, use this flag to remove the input code from the cell.

remove-output.doc: If the argument is a notebook cell, use this flag to remove the output from the cell.

placeholder.doc: A placeholder image when using a notebook cell as the figure contents. This will be shown in place of the Jupyter output until an execution environment is attached. It will also be used in static outputs, such as a PDF output.

no-subfigures.doc: Disallow implicit subfigure creation from child nodes

kind.doc: Override the figures "kind", which changes the enumeration to start counting independently for that kind. For example, `kind: "example"`. The default enumeration and referencing will be the capitalized `kind` followed by a number (e.g. "Example 1").

body.doc: If an argument is provided to the figure directive, the body will be the figure caption. You may also omit the figure directive argument and provide images in the body of the figure, these will be parsed into sub figures.

arg.doc: The URL source (`src`) of the HTML iframe element.

class.doc: Annotate the iframe with a set of space-delimited class names.

label.doc: Label the iframe to be cross-referenced or explicitly linked to.

enumerated.doc: Turn on/off the numbering for the specific iframe

width.doc: The iframe width, in CSS units, for example `50%` or `300px`.

align.doc: The alignment of the iframe in the page. Choose one of `left`, `center` or `right`

title.doc: The title attribute for the iframe element, describing its content for accessibility.

placeholder.doc: A placeholder image for the iframe in static exports.

body.doc: If provided, this will be the iframe caption.

width.doc: The image width, in CSS units, for example `50%` or `300px`.

directives.name: include
directives.doc: Allows you to include the source or parsed version of a separate file into your document tree.

arg.doc: The file path, which is relative to the file from which it was referenced.

class.doc: Annotate the include with a set of space-delimited class names.

label.doc: Label the include to be cross-referenced or explicitly linked to.

enumerated.doc: Turn on/off the numbering for the specific include

literal.doc: Flag the include block as literal, and show the contents as a code block. This can also be set automatically by setting the `language` or using the `literalinclude` directive.

lang.doc: The language of the code to be highlighted as. If set, this automatically changes an `include` into a `literalinclude`.

caption.doc: A parsed caption for the code block.

lineno-start.doc: Start line numbering from a particular value, default is 1. If present, line numbering is activated.

number-lines.doc: Alternative for "lineno-start", turns on line numbering and can be an integer that is the start of the line numbering.

emphasize-lines.doc: Emphasize particular lines (comma-separated numbers which can include ranges), e.g. "3,5,7-9"

filename.doc: Show the filename in addition to the rendered code. The `include` directive will use the filename by default, to turn off this default set the filename to `false`.

start-line.doc: Only the content starting from this line will be included. The first line has index 0 and negative values count from the end.

start-at.doc: Only the content after and including the first occurrence of the specified text in the external data file will be included.

start-after.doc: Only the content after the first occurrence of the specified text in the external data file will be included.

end-line.doc: Only the content up to (but excluding) this line will be included.

end-at.doc: Only the content up to and including the first occurrence of the specified text in the external data file (but after any start-after text) will be included.

end-before.doc: Only the content before the first occurrence of the specified text in the external data file (but after any start-after text) will be included.

lines.doc: Specify exactly which lines to include from the original file, starting at 1. For example, `1,3,5-10,20-` includes the lines 1, 3, 5 to 10 and lines 20 to the last line of the original file.

lineno-match.doc: Display the original line numbers, correct only when the selection consists of contiguous lines.
